canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether a versioned workspace that synchronizes native artifacts, parsed representations, and reviewable staged changes improves knowledge-work agents compared with more restricted workspace views.
StagedWorkspace treats the native workspace W_t as the authoritative state for execution and submission rather than treating parsed representations as independent copies of the artifact.
Parsed records C_t are tied to source paths and content hashes, and a parsed record is current only when its recorded source hash matches the corresponding native workspace file.

The review state Delta_t is derived from changes between the accepted baseline workspace and the current native workspace, so diffs are review views of workspace state rather than separate document copies.
After a mutating tool batch, the system scans file hashes, advances the workspace state, and selectively refreshes parsed records for affected files.
Each staged operation records an actor, target path, base hash, operation type, and payload, allowing the workspace to reject or flag an operation whose base hash no longer matches the target file.

source_anchor.supplement: Appendix A - Commit and Promotion Semantics

canonical_statement: Review diffs are format-aware: the implementation uses line-oriented views for text, row or cell views for spreadsheets, slide-level views for presentations, and before-after previews for binary artifacts.

source_anchor.supplement: Appendix A - Versioned Workspace and Branches

canonical_statement: The agent loop routes search and reading through parsed representations when available while preserving native files for execution, rendering, programmatic editing, and deliverable submission.
Agent execution used an isolated sandbox with 1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, 3 GiB disk, a 30-second default command limit, a 600-second maximum command limit, and a 250-tool-call budget.

The OfficeQA evaluation used 133 questions, including 104 document-only questions and 29 questions requiring web information, over a corpus of about 697 U.S. Treasury Bulletin PDFs spanning 1939 through 2025.

The APEX evaluation used 452 tasks after excluding 28 Investment Banking tasks that depended on unavailable EDGAR external APIs; the benchmark spans 33 professional-work worlds and averages about 166 files per task.

canonical_statement: The read-axis mechanism ablation compares dual parsed-plus-native access, artifact-only access, and parsed-only access while holding the model, prompt, parser, retriever, grader, file tracker, and tool budget fixed.
The review-axis mechanism ablation holds dual artifact access fixed and compares visible versus hidden diff tools on 57 APEX file-editing tasks.
The mechanism ablations used three independent attempts per task and estimated uncertainty with 10,000 bootstrap resamples using seed 20260515; paired comparisons resampled matched task units.

canonical_statement: Residual failures included cases where the agent found the correct source material but still made numerical, table-scope, planning, domain, or rubric mistakes, showing that state management did not remove higher-level reasoning failures.
A parser-sensitivity check on the OfficeQA parsed-only arm found Pass@1 shifts under two percentage points across two parser exports of the same Treasury PDFs.

Early design probes found that presenting parsed companions as a general reading surface could cause over-answering from cached text; the final design instead treats parsed content as a synchronized search-and-retrieval view tied to the native file.
The graders primarily score final answers and deliverables rather than intermediate state-management successes, so they do not directly measure every benefit claimed for the workspace contract.
The paper's hand-coded trajectory analysis is illustrative rather than exhaustive and may be affected by coder variability.

Published complete-system comparison rows are non-paired and differ in attempt budgets, harnesses, retrieval, and parser details, so the paper reserves causal interpretation for the matched mechanism ablations.
Because parser and retriever choices were held fixed in the main mechanism study, the results do not fully separate the workspace state contract from those implementation components.
The evaluated outcome benchmarks do not establish that the proposed state model is the unique or minimal abstraction required for reliable knowledge-work agents.
A substantial residual failure slice remained on APEX, including 188 of 452 tasks that were all-arm-zero for at least one completed model triplet.

The authors conclude that explicit workspace state, synchronized parsed and native views, and reviewable staged changes can improve knowledge-work agent performance while preserving a native artifact as the execution and submission authority.

The paper argues that future agent benchmarks should evaluate acceptance criteria over state transitions and artifact state, not only the final answer, because outcome-only grading misses stale-state and review failures.
Reducto provided in-kind API credits used for the document parser.
The authors state that a sanitized research implementation is planned for GitHub; it was not the production code path used for the reported runs.
The paper states that high-stakes deployments require qualified human review and does not validate the system for clinical or other high-stakes decision making.
